clue.text: Short ball hit over point? Clever!

indicators.note: a ball hit over is knocked about, so the shortened word's letters are rearranged
short means the word ball loses its final letter

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A batter clips a short-pitched ball over point, and the commentator applauds the shot as clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks the last letter and 'hit over' scrambles what is left; 'point' is a compass point, not the fielding position.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone able is capable and skilled, a near synonym of clever.

clue.text: Take away sandwich followed broadcast

parts.note: a sub is a submarine sandwich

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard spoken, and the spoken form is spelt differently

parts.note: to have followed someone is to have tracked them

explanation.surface: Someone orders a takeaway sandwich and then the news bulletin comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals that TRACKED, said aloud, sounds like TRACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To take one number away from another is to perform a subtraction, so the phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Australian native at crease, accruing century in Adelaide initially

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the six words that precede it is taken

explanation.surface: An Australian batter settles in at the crease and builds a century at the Adelaide Oval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian native' tempts towards a cricketer such as a home batter; it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The wattle and many other trees of this genus grow wild in Australia, so it is a native plant.

clue.text: Final resting place in Bath, when injured in action

indicators.note: in means one set of letters goes inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action

indicators.note: injured means the letters of Bath are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: A player injured in action at Bath ends up laid out, perhaps for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when injured' scrambles the city's name and 'in' sets it within the word for action; the definition plays on 'final resting place' usually meaning a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: The bed on which a person dies is, jokingly, where they rest for the last time.

clue.text: Sex good right away, after a stiffener?

indicators.note: after means the next letters follow the word a

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, which in Roman numerals is VI
A stands for away, as in football fixture lists

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark that sex improves straight away after a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Sex is Latin for six, VI; A, then G, R and A after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The drug is taken to bring about and keep an erection, so it is a stiffening agent; the question mark flags the joke.

clue.text: European getting flipper to spin at last

parts.note: a fin is a fish's flipper

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of spin

explanation.surface: A European bowler is given a flipper to spin, a delivery he finally gets to bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Finland is a European, so this is an example of the wider class.

clue.text: Bob cut short-pitched delivery

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a bouncer is a short-pitched ball that rears up at the batter

explanation.surface: A batter ducks under a short ball, or plays a cut shot off it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name or a haircut; it means to spring up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to move up and down lightly, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Family of doctors, not very large one

indicators.note: not means the letters for very large are taken out

parts.note: medicos is informal for doctors
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A family of doctors, none of them particularly big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes OS, the clothing label for outsize; the Medici name itself means doctors in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine banking dynasty that ruled Renaissance Florence is the famous family named.

clue.text: Willing male, adult moving East to India or Australia?

indicators.note: in an across entry east is rightwards, so the adult letter moves later in the word

parts.note: a testate person has made a valid will before dying
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A willing adult man relocates eastwards to India or Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: TESTATE plus M gives TESTATEM; 'moving East' shifts the A two places right.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of those countries fields a national side in the longest form of cricket, so they are examples.

clue.text: Note label on luggage's most essential in city in 21

parts.note: a chit is a short note
a tag is a label

indicators.note: the most essential part of a word is its centre, the single middle letter of luggage

explanation.surface: A note on a luggage label lists only the essentials for a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The port is a major city in the south-east of the country named at 21.

clue.text: Whole female 23 dismissed in the morning, after batting

indicators.note: after puts the batting word in front of the rest

parts.note: a batting side is said to be in
Viola is a girl's name, the heroine of Twelfth Night

indicators.note: dismissed means those letters are sent away from the word

parts.note: the answer to 23 across
AM means in the morning

explanation.surface: A whole women's team was bowled out in the morning session after going in to bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 refers to that answer; dismissing AM from it leaves TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbroken and untouched is entire, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Daughter attending sportsmen's dance in city in 21

parts.note: the haka is the Maori war dance performed by New Zealand rugby players

explanation.surface: A daughter goes along to watch the rugby players perform their dance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital and largest city of the country named at 21.

clue.text: Dead designer returning as Star Wars robot

indicators.note: returning means the designer's name is read backwards

parts.note: Christian Dior was a famous fashion designer

explanation.surface: A late fashion designer comes back to life as a film robot.
explanation.definitionFit: The films call their mechanical servants by this term, a shortening of android.

clue.text: Unruly child put in rival's phone setting

indicators.note: put in means one word goes inside another

parts.note: to rival is to vie; the 's is read as is
a brat is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A naughty child fiddles with a rival's mobile and changes its settings.
explanation.definitionFit: A silent mode makes the handset shake instead of ringing, a familiar option on mobiles.

clue.text: Black English footballer at Stoke City

parts.note: Wilfried Bony, an Ivorian striker, played for Stoke City, an English football club

explanation.surface: A report about an English player turning out for Stoke City.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoke City is a football club in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark tropical wood gives its name to a deep colour, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Beginning to find jumper extremely tight

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper
tight starts and ends with the same letter, so its extreme letter is a single T

explanation.surface: Someone first discovers their jumper fits very tightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater; it is the hopping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The origin or source of something is where it starts, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Run out before Bill bowled first wide

indicators.note: first puts the bowled letter at the front
before puts the run-out letters ahead of the bill

parts.note: B is the scorecard abbreviation for bowled
RO is the scorecard abbreviation for run out
an ad, an advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A cricket scorecard: one batter run out, Bill bowled, and the first delivery a wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wide' looks like the cricket extra; it means extensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something broad is of great width, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Regretted bad running with Moeen

indicators.note: running means the letters of bad and Moeen are set in motion into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone regretted a poor bit of running between the wickets with Moeen Ali.
explanation.walkthrough: Moeen Ali is an England cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament or complain about something is to express regret, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Criminal has no right to be captain

indicators.note: has no means the letter for right is missing

parts.note: a crook is a criminal

explanation.surface: A criminal is barred from taking on the captaincy.
explanation.walkthrough: James Cook, the explorer, is the classic Captain; Alastair Cook also captained England.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval explorer was Captain James Cook, so the rank is attached to the name.

clue.text: Against hiding tasteless articles being carried by XI getting award

indicators.note: hiding means the outer word conceals the others within it

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: being carried by puts the tasteless goods between the letters of the eleven

parts.note: XI is eleven, which written as 11 looks like a pair of the letter I
tat is cheap tasteless goods

explanation.surface: A cricket eleven, laden with cheap trophies, is up against it for a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: XI is eleven, and eleven written as 11 resembles two capital I letters; 'being carried by' and 'hiding' are both container signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal mention for bravery or merit is an honour given out, so it counts as an award.

clue.text: Fix cover back on front of book

indicators.note: on front of puts the turned word ahead of the book
back means the cover word is read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is the Jane Austen novel

explanation.surface: Instructions to repair a book by putting its cover back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' looks like a repair verb; it is the noun, a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fix is a predicament, a situation offering only awkward choices, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Number one amongst cricket sides

indicators.note: amongst means the numeral sits between the two side names

parts.note: leg and on are both names for the same side of a cricket field
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single player is shared between two cricket teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a figure; it is a vast host.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion is a huge multitude, so 'their number is legion' uses it for a great quantity.

clue.text: Cricket club try losing runs? That's crazy

parts.note: a bat is the club used in cricket

indicators.note: losing means the letter for runs drops out of try

parts.note: R is the scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket club attempts a run chase without scoring any runs, which is madness.
explanation.definitionFit: Batty is informal for eccentric or mad, a synonym of crazy.

clue.text: Kill using tear gas internally

indicators.note: internally means the gas symbol goes inside the word for tear

parts.note: a tear is a bead of liquid from the eye
He is the chemical symbol of helium, a gas

explanation.surface: Someone is killed with tear gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' looks like a rip; it is a teardrop.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting off someone's head is a way to put them to death, so the verbs overlap.

clue.text: Boycott pleased he's played for 9 23

parts.note: to boycott is to ban, with a nod to the cricketer Geoffrey Boycott
glad means pleased

indicators.note: played means the letters of he's are rearranged

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott, the Yorkshire batter, is pleased to have played for his country.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 23 means the answer to the linked clue at 9 and 23.
explanation.definitionFit: The country has played the long form of international cricket since 2000, so it is one such national side.

clue.text: Further article by group of players

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra, a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A further newspaper article mentions a group of players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' suggests cricketers; they are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words add something more, as in 'he also came', so they are synonyms.

clue.text: See 9
Sailor boy not yet up and about

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young sailor is still lying in his bunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone still lying in bed has not risen for the day, so the phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Maybe adds Wood to side, starting after second draw

indicators.note: starting after puts the draw word straight after the abbreviation for second

parts.note: to toke is to draw on a joint; here in the third person

explanation.surface: An England captain adds fast bowler Mark Wood to the team, then a second draw follows.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Stokes captained England, so he might pick Mark Wood; 'adds wood' also suggests feeding a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeding fuel into a fire is the verb's ordinary sense, and Ben Stokes as captain picks players.

clue.text: Very beginning of year over in Scandinavian setting

indicators.note: setting means the Scandinavian forms a surround for the other letters

parts.note: a Dane is from Denmark, a Scandinavian country
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: The very start of a year that has passed in a Scandinavian setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase denotes the first moment of something, the starting point, matching the very beginning.
